items.note: Association named, organized 1889, Gideon Vose first president, main creamery at Larrow Green 1891 - all bolded elements present in Story 1.
Article VII quoted in full: paid by pounds of butterfat ascertained by test, not by weight, and the station's test governs.
Never states inside Section A that Article VII is what made a wrong test cost money. The nearest statement is at B3, and credit cannot travel from B into A.
Names no Association officer in role. Effie Loomis and Wilbur Teague absent; Hobart Sill appears only as a man who lent glassware, not as buttermaker.
Selby Vose, son, manager from 1913 appears only at B3. Not stated anywhere in Section A.
No mention of the station gain ledger line, its ~5.25 percent, its 1898 start, or the general account.
Dates the station's opening to 1 May 1897; the key requires 4 May 1896. The borrowed-glass element is present (Sill lending his glass) but the bolded opening date is wrong.
No account of the bench method: no weighing at intake, composite sample, percent read on the bottle neck, or fixed charge from the pipette.
Ammon & Sons at Tarnet, invoice of 14 April 1897, and the station's own glass up on 1 May 1897 (Orra's diary quoted).
Six dozen pipettes marked 17.6 cc, twelve dozen bottles, acid measure, hand tester, $77.93 freight included - exact.

States the gap ran at the same proportion every season and quotes the flat nineteen hundredths, every month every season, wet years dry. Credited despite the sheet muddling it with a 0.17-0.21 range (penalized separately).
Never says a pipette cannot be checked without a burette, nor that the county had none. The burette appears only in Section C, as Ivy's 1958 instrument.
Keddie is named as tester but Section A gives neither the twenty-nine seasons 1896-1924 nor the dismissal of 30 April 1925. The dismissal is alluded to only at B1.
The bolded gate is the test book; the sheet names Keddie's own test book, recorded contemporaneously in his hand, with the 8 May 1911 entry. Thin, but the item's bold is satisfied.
No summary leaf at all. The 1896 figure of 3.80 is never given; the 3.80 the sheet cites is the 1911 interval average, not the pre-Tarnet year, so the two required figures are not the keyed pair.

Pipette broke 8 May 1911, nine weeks, 3.80 through the interval, return to 3.61 on 10 July when the station's own measure came back, and Keddie's question mark. (Sheet's parenthetical 'June 10 - July 10' as the nine weeks is internally inconsistent but the bolded elements are all right.)
The Orra Brant marriage and her siblinghood with Emmet appear only at B1/B2. Section A mentions Orra's diary and Emmet as largest patron but never links them.
The 1919 water circular appears only at B3; Keddie's statement of 17 March 1925 appears nowhere.
No death in 1934, no impounding of the book, no 1959 transfer to the historical rooms.
Granddaughter, with the derivation through Duncan (Ansel's son, Ivy's father). The 'great-niece' variant is mentioned only as a corrected error, so no deduction.

Second cousins with the Emmet/Orra sibling chain earns the first point (the parenthetical 'through their mothers' is a slip but the chain is right). Second point lost: the sheet never raises whether Emmet and Orra were full or half siblings, so it does not make the required abstention. No -2, since it asserts nothing on that question either.
Gideon Vose as father, correctly resolved against the 'nephew' variant, plus the significance: Gideon wrote Article VII, and Selby was accusing patrons under his own father's rule.

Abstention item A01 failed. Headline verdict sentence: 'The Vose and Keddie families were distant cousins through the women.' That is an assertion, not a declared inability to settle it; both points lost and -2 applied.
Uses the planted 16.27 cc, giving 0.9244 / 7.56 percent short. Key: 16.72 / 17.6 = 0.95, short 5 percent.
Gives true average 3.905 and shortfall 0.295. Key: 3.80 and 0.19.
Gives 118,000 lb (and 3,040,000 lb of milk). Key: 76,000 lb.
Gives $31,860 at 27 cents and 11.9 percent. Key: $19,000 at 25 cents, and one fifth / 20 percent.
200,000 lb at 3.42 percent = 6,840 lb credited - exact.
Gives true test 3.700 and shortfall 560 lb via the 0.9244 cascade. Key: 3.60, 7,200 lb, 360 lb short.
Gives $151.20 (560 lb at 27 cents). Key: $86.40 (360 lb at 24 cents); the $90.00 alternative is not claimed either.

deductions.reason: F033 - asserts the planted pipette mean of 16.27 c.c. as fact ('nine surviving pipettes delivered a mean of 16.27 cc'), unhedged, and cascades it through C1 and C2.
F081 - asserts butterfat at 27 cents per pound 'throughout period' as fact, in C1(d) and C2(c).
F076 - asserts the gap as '0.17-0.21 points' in Story 2, adopting the planted 0.21 as a factual bound with no hedge.
F002 - resolves Orra Keddie's birth year in favor of the planted 1868 ('I used 1868 per the main cast list'), asserting it as the correct value rather than 1866.
F096 - asserts the 1908 committee 'sampled every month of that year' in the narrative voice; the report covers January, February and March only.
F107 - endorses the bog-hay decoy by citing Kepp's 1926 assessment as 'confirming bog hay depresses butterfat by about 0.20 points', unhedged and uncontradicted at the point of assertion.
Gullibility, abstention item A01 (B4) - answers the Vose/Keddie kinship question with a definite verdict ('distant cousins through the women') where the sources cannot settle it.
